title: Ambient diagonal purity and its normalized base-change map
statement:
Let $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$ with $\ell$ prime [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $Y$ be an excellent Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible and $h:X\to Y$ a separated smooth morphism of finite type and pure relative dimension $r\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings; excellence is [def-exc-excellent-ring]. On ordinary unbounded etale $A$-module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], use compact support [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and its ambient right adjoint $h^\times$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Put $\omega_h=h^\times A_Y$. Define $A_T(1)=\mu_{\ell^m,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^m}A$ for any $m$ with $\ell^mA=0$, its tensor powers $A_T(r)$, and $M(r)=M\otimes_A^LA_T(r)$; these definitions are independent of $m$.

The diagonal-class/deformation-to-the-normal-bundle construction gives an orientation $a_h:A_X(r)[2r]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_h$. More precisely its inverse is the diagonal restriction $\omega_h\cong\Delta^*\omega_{p_1}$, followed by deformation of the diagonal section to the zero section of $T_{X/Y}$, followed by restriction of the inverse Kummer-normalized vector-bundle purity map. Here $p_1:X\times_YX\to X$ and $\Delta:X\to X\times_YX$. For every $M\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the tensor map defined as the $Rh_!\dashv h^\times$ transpose of inverse projection followed by the counit gives a natural isomorphism
$$\gamma_h(M):h^*M(r)[2r]\xrightarrow{\sim}h^\times M.$$
There is no boundedness, constructibility or finite-Tor hypothesis on $M$.

For a Cartesian base change $v:Y'\to Y$ with $Y'$ excellent Noetherian, let $u:X'\to X$, $h':X'\to Y'$ be its projections and $B:v^*Rh_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh'_!u^*$ compact-support base change. The canonical exceptional comparison $c_M:u^*h^\times M\to h'^\times v^*M$ is the transpose of $v^*\epsilon_h(M)\circ B^{-1}$. Under canonical pullback and twist identifications,
$$c_M\circ u^*\gamma_h(M)=\gamma_{h'}(v^*M).$$
The orientations, tensor maps and adjoint smooth traces therefore commute with this base change and composition; for $r=0$ they are the etale adjunction maps. This includes base change to separably closed fields, arbitrary extensions of such fields, and geometric fibres of excellent traits.

For all $L,M\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the exceptional internal-Hom comparison
$$H_h:h^\times R\mathcal Hom_A(L,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(h^*L,h^\times M)$$
is an isomorphism. It is specified by the pairing $h^\times R\mathcal Hom_A(L,M)\otimes h^*L\to h^\times(R\mathcal Hom_A(L,M)\otimes L)\to h^\times M$, where the first arrow is the counit-defined exceptional tensor map and the second is evaluation. Internal Hom and tensor have their ordinary unbounded meanings [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-kun-derived-tensor]. This specifies the evaluation normalization of the isomorphism as well as its direction.

source.place: Finite-stage argument with arbitrary finite coefficients; sk-prop-sp-orientation.proof.md (diagonal, deformation, vector bundle), sk-prop-sp-purity-bc-factors.md. Agent extension to the ordinary ambient excellent-Noetherian setting, retaining the lecture-notes route; Scholze, Six-Functor Formalisms, Lecture V, Theorem 5.5 and its base-change conclusion.
